title: Principality of Capua
capsule: The Principality of Capua originated as a Lombard gastaldate within the Duchy of Benevento; Atenulf I established independent princely rule in 887 and briefly united the southern Lombard lands by seizing Benevento in 899. Under Pandulf Ironhead (r. 943-981) the principality dominated the Terra di Lavoro and at times held Benevento and the Duchy of Spoleto. Norman mercenaries founded the County of Aversa in 1030 at Capuan invitation, beginning the erosion of Lombard authority, and in 1058 Richard of Aversa captured Capua from its last Lombard prince, bringing the principality under Norman rule.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The principality's core territory is well documented from Lombard chronicles and papal correspondence; peripheral boundary adjustments with Benevento and Salerno are reconstructed from narrative rather than cartographic sources.
